blocks.en: 📖 The Gospel of John — Unit 3: Living Water
blocks.es_reference: 📖 El Evangelio de Juan — Unidad 3: Agua Viva

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: "Whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst. But the water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life." — John 4:14 (NKJV)
blocks.es_reference: ⚡ "Mas el que bebiere del agua que yo le daré, no tendrá sed jamás; sino que el agua que yo le daré será en él una fuente de agua que salte para vida eterna." — Juan 4:14 (RVG)

blocks.en: Introduction — A Divine Partnership
blocks.es_reference: Introducción — Una Asociación Divina

blocks.en: Imagine a garden full of vibrant flowers, lush plants, and towering trees. God creates the life in the plants; He sends the sunshine and the rain. But the gardener must still nurture and trim and fertilize and weed, or the true beauty is never unveiled. Our lives are like that garden. Jesus offered the Samaritan woman living water — He offered her Himself — but the real beauty of her story was unveiled when she ran and shared the Christ she had only just met. Again and again Scripture shows this lovely symmetry: God provides salvation and the power of His Spirit, and then God works through us to finish His purpose. "It is God who works in you both to will and to do for His good pleasure" (Philippians 2:13). That is the Divine Partnership, and this chapter is its picture.
blocks.es_reference: Imagine un jardín lleno de flores vibrantes, plantas exuberantes y árboles imponentes. Dios crea la vida en las plantas; él envía el sol y la lluvia. Pero el jardinero aún debe cuidar, podar, fertilizar y desmalezar, o la verdadera belleza jamás se revela. Nuestras vidas son como ese jardín. Jesús ofreció a la mujer samaritana agua viva — se ofreció a sí mismo — pero la verdadera belleza de su historia se reveló cuando ella corrió y compartió al Cristo que apenas acababa de conocer. Una y otra vez la Escritura muestra esta hermosa simetría: Dios provee la salvación y el poder de su Espíritu, y luego Dios obra a través de nosotros para cumplir su propósito. ⚡ "Porque Dios es el que en vosotros produce así el querer como el hacer, por su buena voluntad" (Filipenses 2:13). Esa es la Asociación Divina, y este capítulo es su cuadro.

blocks.en: I. The Woman at the Well
blocks.es_reference: I. La mujer junto al pozo

blocks.en: Jesus, wearied from His journey, sat down by Jacob's well about the sixth hour while His disciples went into the town to buy food. A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Everything about that meeting was a wall a respectable rabbi would not climb. She was a Samaritan, a half-Jew — and the Jews and the Samaritans despised one another. She was a woman, and the teachers did not speak with women in public. And she was, by the town's reckoning, a great sinner; she would prove to have had five husbands, and the man she lived with then was not her husband. She was, as we would say, a hopeless case. Yet Jesus opened the conversation Himself: "Give Me a drink." The Maker of the spring asked a sinner for a cup of water, so that He might give her a fountain.
blocks.es_reference: Jesús, cansado del camino, se sentó junto al pozo de Jacob como a la hora sexta mientras sus discípulos iban al pueblo a comprar comida. Una mujer de Samaria vino a sacar agua. Todo en aquel encuentro era un muro que un rabí respetable no escalaría. Ella era samaritana, mitad judía — y judíos y samaritanos se despreciaban mutuamente. Era mujer, y los maestros no hablaban con mujeres en público. Y era, según el cálculo del pueblo, una gran pecadora; resultaría que había tenido cinco maridos, y el hombre con quien vivía entonces no era su marido. Era, como diríamos, un caso perdido. Sin embargo, Jesús mismo abrió la conversación: "Dame de beber." El Hacedor del manantial pidió a una pecadora una taza de agua, para poder darle una fuente.

blocks.en: II. The Living Water
blocks.es_reference: II. El agua viva

blocks.en: "If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, 'Give Me a drink,' you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water" (John 4:10). She heard only the well at her feet — You have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. But Jesus was speaking of another water altogether. "Whoever drinks of this water will thirst again, but whoever drinks of the water that I shall give him will never thirst. The water that I shall give him will become in him a fountain of water springing up into everlasting life" (John 4:13–14). The world's water always runs out; you drink, and within hours you are thirsty again. The water Christ gives does not sit in a cistern to be rationed — it springs up, it overflows, it becomes a fountain inside the one who drinks.
blocks.es_reference: ⚡ "Si conocieras el don de Dios, y quién es el que te dice: Dame de beber; tú le pedirías a él, y él te daría agua viva" (Juan 4:10). Ella solo oyó el pozo a sus pies — no tienes con qué sacarla, y el pozo es hondo. Pero Jesús hablaba de otra agua del todo distinta. ⚡ "Cualquiera que bebiere de esta agua, volverá a tener sed; mas el que bebiere del agua que yo le daré, no tendrá sed jamás; sino que el agua que yo le daré será en él una fuente de agua que salte para vida eterna" (Juan 4:13–14). El agua del mundo siempre se acaba; usted bebe, y en pocas horas vuelve a tener sed. El agua que Cristo da no queda en una cisterna para racionarse — brota, se desborda, se vuelve una fuente dentro del que bebe.

blocks.en: Some years ago I traveled in the Canadian province of Ontario and made sure to drive and see Niagara Falls, on the border of Canada and the United States — the grandest waterfall in all of North America, where millions of gallons pour over the edge every single minute and never, ever stop. That is a faint picture of the fullness Jesus offered that woman. He offered her Himself. Salvation, and a purpose for living, are found in Him alone, and they never run dry.
blocks.es_reference: Hace algunos años viajé por la provincia canadiense de Ontario y me aseguré de ir a ver las Cataratas del Niágara, en la frontera de Canadá y los Estados Unidos — la cascada más grandiosa de toda América del Norte, donde millones de galones caen por el borde cada minuto y nunca, jamás, se detienen. Ese es un débil cuadro de la plenitud que Jesús ofreció a aquella mujer. Le ofreció a sí mismo. La salvación, y un propósito para vivir, se hallan solo en él, y nunca se secan.

blocks.en: The world's water always runs out. The water Christ gives springs up — it overflows, it becomes a fountain inside the one who drinks.
blocks.es_reference: El agua del mundo siempre se acaba. El agua que Cristo da brota — se desborda, se vuelve una fuente dentro del que bebe.

blocks.en: Every one of us was made with a thirst that no well of this world can fill. We carry our buckets to the cisterns of money, of pleasure, of approval, of one more relationship, and we drink, and for an hour we are satisfied — and then the old dryness creeps back, because those wells were never deep enough for a soul. The woman at Jacob's well had been to that kind of cistern five times over, and the man she lived with then was a sixth bucket let down into an empty well. Jesus did not scold her thirst; He offered to end it. And He offers the same to us. The ache you cannot quite name, the restlessness that no achievement finally quiets, is the soul's cry for the only water that satisfies. His invitation has not changed in two thousand years: drink of Me, and you will never thirst again.
blocks.es_reference: Cada uno de nosotros fue hecho con una sed que ningún pozo de este mundo puede llenar. Llevamos nuestros cubos a las cisternas del dinero, del placer, de la aprobación, de una relación más, y bebemos, y por una hora quedamos satisfechos — y luego la vieja sequedad regresa, porque aquellos pozos nunca fueron lo bastante hondos para un alma. La mujer junto al pozo de Jacob había ido a esa clase de cisterna cinco veces, y el hombre con quien vivía entonces era un sexto cubo bajado a un pozo vacío. Jesús no regañó su sed; le ofreció ponerle fin. Y nos ofrece lo mismo. El anhelo que no logra nombrar, la inquietud que ningún logro acalla del todo, es el clamor del alma por la única agua que satisface. Su invitación no ha cambiado en dos mil años: bebe de mí, y no tendrás sed jamás.

blocks.en: III. In Spirit and in Truth
blocks.es_reference: III. En espíritu y en verdad

blocks.en: Then He touched the wound. "Go, call your husband, and come here." "I have no husband." "You have well said... for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband." He did not shame her; He simply showed her that He already knew everything, and still was offering her the fountain. Seeing a prophet before her, she raised the old quarrel of worship: our fathers worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say Jerusalem is the place. Jesus lifted the whole question to higher ground: "God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth" (John 4:24). True worship is not finally a matter of the right mountain or the right building, but of the heart and the Spirit and the truth of God. And then, to this woman — a Samaritan, an outsider, a sinner — He said what He had said plainly to no one else: "I who speak to you am He." The first soul to hear Jesus openly name Himself the Messiah was a woman at a well at noon.
blocks.es_reference: Entonces tocó la herida. "Ve, llama a tu marido, y ven acá." "No tengo marido." "Bien has dicho... porque cinco maridos has tenido, y el que ahora tienes no es tu marido." No la avergonzó; sencillamente le mostró que ya lo sabía todo, y que aún le ofrecía la fuente. Viendo a un profeta ante ella, ella levantó la vieja disputa del culto: nuestros padres adoraron en este monte, mas vosotros los judíos decís que Jerusalén es el lugar. Jesús elevó toda la cuestión a un terreno más alto: ⚡ "Dios es Espíritu; y los que le adoran, en espíritu y en verdad es necesario que adoren" (Juan 4:24). La verdadera adoración no es finalmente cuestión del monte correcto ni del edificio correcto, sino del corazón y del Espíritu y de la verdad de Dios. Y entonces, a esta mujer — samaritana, marginada, pecadora — le dijo lo que a nadie más había dicho tan claramente: "Yo soy, el que habla contigo." La primera alma en oír a Jesús nombrarse abiertamente el Mesías fue una mujer junto a un pozo al mediodía.

blocks.en: IV. The First Evangelist: Come and See
blocks.es_reference: IV. La primera evangelista: Ven y ve

blocks.en: What she did next preaches its own sermon. "The woman then left her waterpot, went her way into the city, and said to the men, 'Come, see a Man who told me all things that I ever did. Could this be the Christ?'" (John 4:28–29). She left the very waterpot she had come for — the old thirst forgotten in the new fountain — and ran to the same townspeople who knew her reputation. She could not have walked anyone through a set of spiritual laws. But she could say two words: come, see. And they came. "Many of the Samaritans of that city believed in Him because of the word of the woman" (John 4:39), and then many more believed because they heard Him for themselves, and said, "Now we believe... and we know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world" (John 4:42).
blocks.es_reference: Lo que hizo después predica su propio sermón. ⚡ "Entonces la mujer dejó su cántaro, y fue a la ciudad, y dijo a los hombres: Venid, ved un hombre que me ha dicho todo cuanto he hecho. ¿No es éste el Cristo?" (Juan 4:28–29). Dejó el mismo cántaro por el que había venido — la vieja sed olvidada en la nueva fuente — y corrió a los mismos del pueblo que conocían su reputación. No habría podido guiar a nadie por un conjunto de leyes espirituales. Pero podía decir dos palabras: venid, ved. Y vinieron. ⚡ "Y muchos de los samaritanos de aquella ciudad creyeron en él por la palabra de la mujer" (Juan 4:39), y luego muchos más creyeron porque le oyeron a él mismo, y decían: "ya no creemos por tu dicho... y sabemos que verdaderamente éste es el Cristo, el Salvador del mundo" (Juan 4:42).

blocks.en: Mark the contrast John quietly draws. The disciples had gone into that same town — trained men, three years under the Lord Himself, the most qualified evangelists on earth — and they came back with bread and no converts; there is no sign they spoke to a soul. The first evangelist in Samaria was one grateful, excited sinner. The living water must have been sparkling water, for it came bubbling up out of her life.
blocks.es_reference: Note el contraste que Juan dibuja en silencio. Los discípulos habían ido a ese mismo pueblo — hombres entrenados, tres años bajo el Señor mismo, los evangelistas más calificados de la tierra — y volvieron con pan y sin convertidos; no hay señal de que hablaran con un alma. La primera evangelista en Samaria fue una pecadora agradecida y emocionada. El agua viva debió ser agua chispeante, pues brotaba burbujeando de su vida.

blocks.en: V. The Fields Are White
blocks.es_reference: V. Los campos están blancos

blocks.en: When the disciples urged Him to eat, Jesus said, "My food is to do the will of Him who sent Me, and to finish His work" (John 4:34). Then He pointed to the Samaritans even then streaming out of the town toward Him: "Lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already white for harvest" (John 4:35). One sows, another reaps, and "he who reaps receives wages... that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together" (John 4:36). There is the Divine Partnership again: Jesus had sown in one woman by a well, and already a whole village was ripening. God gives the increase, but He is pleased to let us carry the seed and swing the sickle, and to share the joy of the harvest.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando los discípulos le rogaron que comiera, Jesús dijo: "Mi comida es que haga la voluntad del que me envió, y que acabe su obra" (Juan 4:34). Luego señaló a los samaritanos que ya entonces salían del pueblo hacia él: ⚡ "Alzad vuestros ojos y mirad las regiones, porque ya están blancas para la siega" (Juan 4:35). Uno siembra, otro siega, y "el que siega recibe salario... para que el que siembra goce juntamente con el que siega" (Juan 4:36). Ahí está otra vez la Asociación Divina: Jesús había sembrado en una mujer junto a un pozo, y ya toda una aldea maduraba. Dios da el crecimiento, pero se complace en dejarnos llevar la semilla y empuñar la hoz, y compartir el gozo de la siega.

blocks.en: VI. Every Believer on the Team
blocks.es_reference: VI. Cada creyente en el equipo

blocks.en: People sometimes imagine there is only one kind of evangelist. There are many, and every believer belongs to the team. There is the mass evangelist — I once sat in a Billy Graham crusade and watched thousands stream forward. There is the defender of the faith, the apologist — men like Lee Strobel and Josh McDowell, or Nabeel Qureshi, who reasoned his way out of Islam into Christ and then spent his short life defending the faith. There is the serving evangelist, like Barnabas the son of encouragement, whose compassion gave weight to his words. There is the tract evangelist: I was told of a paralyzed man named J. D. Fore who could move almost nothing, yet stamped gospel tracts by gripping a rubber stamp in his teeth and, with his mother's help, mailed them to soldiers across the world — and his wall filled with letters from men saved through those tracts. There is the timid or "come and see" evangelist, like the little white-haired man on George Street in Sydney who asked passersby one quiet question — "If you died today, where would you be?" — and never knew, until late in life, how many he had sent to Christ. And there is the invitational evangelist, the Samaritan woman herself, who only said, "Come and see." You may never preach to thousands or argue a skeptic to his knees. But you can say, "Come and see." Have you drunk of the living water? Then leave the waterpot, and go.
blocks.es_reference: A veces se imagina que hay un solo tipo de evangelista. Hay muchos, y cada creyente pertenece al equipo. Está el evangelista masivo — una vez me senté en una cruzada de Billy Graham y vi a miles pasar al frente. Está el defensor de la fe, el apologista — hombres como Lee Strobel y Josh McDowell, o Nabeel Qureshi, que razonó su salida del islam hacia Cristo y luego pasó su corta vida defendiendo la fe. Está el evangelista del servicio, como Bernabé el hijo de consolación, cuya compasión daba peso a sus palabras. Está el evangelista de folletos: me contaron de un hombre paralítico llamado J. D. Fore que casi no podía mover nada, pero estampaba tratados del evangelio sujetando un sello de goma con los dientes y, con ayuda de su madre, los enviaba a soldados por todo el mundo — y su pared se llenó de cartas de hombres salvos por aquellos tratados. Está el evangelista tímido o de "ven y ve", como el hombrecito de cabello blanco en George Street, en Sídney, que hacía a los transeúntes una pregunta callada — "Si murieras hoy, ¿dónde estarías?" — y nunca supo, hasta ya anciano, a cuántos había enviado a Cristo. Y está el evangelista invitador, la misma mujer samaritana, que solo dijo: "Venid y ved." Quizá usted nunca predique a miles ni lleve a un escéptico de rodillas con argumentos. Pero puede decir: "Ven y ve." ¿Ha bebido del agua viva? Entonces deje el cántaro, y vaya.

sa.prompt: Explain what Jesus meant by "living water" (John 4:10–14) and how it differs from well water.
sa.model: Living water is not the water in Jacob's well but Christ Himself and the life He gives. Ordinary well water leaves you thirsty again within hours, but Jesus said the water He gives becomes in a person a fountain of water springing up to everlasting life. It does not sit in a cistern to be rationed; it overflows and never runs dry. The gift of God is Christ, and whoever drinks of Him finds salvation and a purpose that the world's water can never supply.

sa.prompt: Describe the barriers Jesus crossed to reach the Samaritan woman, and what this shows.
sa.model: Jesus crossed three walls a respectable rabbi would not climb. She was a Samaritan, and Jews and Samaritans despised one another, so race was a barrier. She was a woman, and teachers did not speak with women in public, so gender was a barrier. And she was a known sinner with five former husbands, so her reputation was a barrier. That Jesus deliberately reached across all of these to this outcast shows that the living water is for the least likely, and no one is too far gone for Him to seek and save.

sa.prompt: Explain "God is Spirit, and those who worship Him must worship in spirit and truth" (John 4:23–24).
sa.model: When the woman asked whether the right place to worship was Mount Gerizim or Jerusalem, Jesus lifted the question higher. Because God is Spirit, true worship is not finally a matter of the correct mountain or building but of the heart, offered in spirit and in truth. To worship in spirit is to worship from the inner person moved by the Holy Spirit, and to worship in truth is to worship according to the truth God has revealed. The Father seeks such worshipers, so right worship is about a renewed heart, not merely a location.

sa.prompt: How did Jesus reveal Himself as Messiah here, and why is it striking that He did so to this woman?
sa.model: When the woman spoke of the coming Messiah, Jesus said plainly, I who speak to you am He. It is striking because the first soul to whom He openly declared His messiahship was not a ruler or a priest but a Samaritan woman, an outsider and a sinner, met at a well at noon. He revealed Himself most clearly to the least likely person, which shows the reach of His grace and overturns every expectation about who is worthy to receive the truth about Christ.

sa.prompt: Describe how the Samaritan woman became the town's first evangelist ("come and see").
sa.model: Once she was convinced Jesus was the Christ, the woman left her waterpot and ran into the town, telling the men, Come, see a Man who told me all I ever did; is this not the Christ? She could not have led anyone through a formal presentation, but she could give a simple invitation and her own witness. Many of the townspeople believed because of her word and then came to hear Jesus for themselves. She is the first evangelist in Samaria, an invitational evangelist whose changed life bubbled over like the living water.

sa.prompt: Explain the "Divine Partnership" taught from John 4:34–38 and Philippians 2:13.
sa.model: The Divine Partnership means that God provides salvation and the power of His Spirit, and then is pleased to work through us to finish His purpose. Jesus said one sows and another reaps, and the sower and reaper rejoice together in the harvest. He had sown in one woman at a well, and already a whole village was ripening for the reaping. Philippians 2:13 says it is God who works in us both to will and to do, so the increase is God's, yet He lets us carry the seed and swing the sickle and share His joy.

sa.prompt: Explain "the fields are already white for harvest" (John 4:35).
sa.model: Jesus told the disciples to lift up their eyes and look, for the fields were already white for harvest. He was pointing to the Samaritans even then streaming out of the town toward Him, ripe souls ready to be gathered. The lesson is that the harvest is not in some distant future but now, all around us, and the laborer must open his eyes to see it. Where we might see only an unlikely town, Jesus saw a field ready to reap.

sa.prompt: Why is the contrast between the woman and the silent disciples significant?
sa.model: The disciples had gone into the very same town; they were trained men who had spent three years with the Lord and were the most qualified evangelists on earth, yet they came back with bread and there is no sign they told a single soul about Jesus. The woman, of the wrong race and the wrong reputation, immediately ran and told the town. The contrast shows that zeal born of gratitude can do more than training without it, and that God often uses the unlikely and the freshly saved while the qualified stay silent.

sa.prompt: Describe the different kinds of evangelists and the truth they teach about the church.
sa.model: There is not one kind of evangelist but many, and every believer is on the team. There is the mass evangelist who preaches to thousands, the apologist or defender of the faith who answers the skeptic, the serving evangelist whose compassion gives weight to his words, the tract evangelist who hands out the gospel in print, the timid come-and-see evangelist who asks one quiet question, and the invitational evangelist like the Samaritan woman who simply says, come and see. The truth is that no one is excused; each believer has a part to play in reaching others for Christ.

sa.prompt: What does it mean that salvation and purpose are found only in Christ, the Living Water?
sa.model: Jesus offered the woman not merely advice or religion but Himself, the Living Water, and said that whoever drinks of Him will never thirst again. This means that the deepest thirst of the human heart is satisfied only in Christ; the world's wells run dry, but He becomes a fountain springing up to eternal life. Salvation and a true purpose for living are found in Him alone, so the answer to our restlessness is not a better mountain, a better marriage, or a fuller cup, but the Savior who gives the water that overflows forever.
